claims.claim: Morgan Stanley projects $2.9T of cumulative global data-center capex 2025-2028 ($1.3T infrastructure + $1.6T IT hardware), with a $1.5T external financing gap after ~$1.4T of hyperscaler self-funding

McKinsey's most commonly cited figure is $6.7T (or $7T) of global data-center capex by 2030; $8T appears only as the upper bound of a $3-8T AI-capacity demand scenario range, not a standalone McKinsey headline estimate
USD.AI protocol TVL peaked at $686.9M on 2026-01-01 and stood at $177.1M on 2026-08-16 per DefiLlama's API, a 74% decline -- roughly double the 37% decline Arete Capital cites

USD.AI's own app dashboard (app.usd.ai/chip) shows TVL of $432.4M as of 2026-08-21, closely matching Arete Capital's cited $430M -- while Stablewatch's independent sUSDai tracker shows $299.8M, illustrating that three trackers using different methodologies produce three materially different TVL figures for the same protocol

USD.AI's own H1 2026 Lighthouse report discloses $202-205M of deployed/closed loans and $283M of total collateral across 13 active loans, well short of the 'approaching $500M' loan book Arete Capital cites
QumulusAI's SEC S-1/A filing shows only $4.3M drawn against its $500M USD.AI facility as of February 2026, despite the company announcing delivery of 1,144 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs under that facility

Loan-book growth since May 2026 traces mainly to new borrowers -- Duos Edge AI ($98.1M, the protocol's single largest loan), NexGen Cloud ($34M) and Crucible Capital ($26.8M) -- rather than Sharon AI or QumulusAI scaling their original facilities

Bleecker Street Research's April 30, 2026 short report on SharonAI (SHAZ) alleges its $1.25B ESDS contract requires ~$250M/year in payments against ESDS's FY25 revenue of $39.9M (6.3x) and requires a $140M letter of credit against ESDS's total assets of $69.5M, and that ESDS's Indian data-sovereignty obligations may bar it from using Australian-based compute

Sharon AI reported 212MW of secured AI Factory capacity as of its August 13, 2026 Q2 earnings call (up from 132MW guidance), plus new $373M and ~$950M customer cloud-service agreements, none of which is a disclosed incremental drawdown on the USD.AI facility beyond its initial ~$65M tranche

USD.AI's Q2 2026 annualized DAO ARR reached $30M per its own Lighthouse report (up from $4.0M in Q1 2026 and $1.1M in 2025), while DefiLlama's independently tracked trailing-twelve-month fee total is only about $7.0M annualized -- roughly a 4x gap between the self-reported forward run-rate and the independently tracked trailing actual

CHIP hit a fresh all-time low of $0.02163 on 2026-08-09 (78% below its April 23, 2026 all-time high of $0.1402) before bouncing to roughly $0.028-0.031 by August 21, 2026; market cap is roughly $56-62M and FDV roughly $293-310M, both down from May 2026 levels ($108.6M market cap / $542.8M FDV)
No governance proposal addressing the April 21, 2027 CHIP unlock cliff (extension, buyback, or OTC clearing facility) was found as of August 21, 2026

The specialist GPU-collateralized private-credit market is independently sized at roughly $20-30B in 2025-2026, with institutional lenders (Blackstone, Ares) pricing at SOFR+450-700bps -- about 100x smaller than the '$2T GPU debt middle market' framing implies

Traditional private-credit lenders already serve mid-sized/growth-stage neocloud operators at comparable or larger deal sizes: Upper90 ($225M to Crusoe), Victory Park Capital ($175M to Crusoe), and Macquarie (up to $10B facility for FluidStack, backstopped by a $6.7B Google contract)

Barker (product-branded 'Barkr') is a single AI hardware-valuation company -- not two conflated entities -- that launched its USD.AI GPU-loan coverage backed by Munich Re's Great Lakes Insurance SE on 2026-02-06, structured so an 80%-of-valuation warranty equals full outstanding principal at USD.AI's 80% max LTV cap

Arete Capital launched in April 2024 targeting a $20M first fund split 50/50 between venture and liquid token investments; both the CHIP thesis's named authors (McKenna and Daveeemor) are Arete Capital personnel, not an independent outside co-author, and no CHIP/USDai/sUSDai position disclosure was located in any indexed source

McKenna has a documented pattern of publishing a bullish public token thesis and later disclosing he personally bought the token off the back of it: an October 2025 HYPE thesis preceded a disclosed purchase at $33; HYPE later peaked near $76-77 in June 2026 before pulling back to about $59, short of McKenna's stated $100 target

Independent analyst Pine Analytics valued CHIP's launch FDV at 1.2x Ethena's FDV/TVL multiple and 2.9x Maple Finance's despite far lower loan utilization (~10% of TVL deployed at the time), implying compression scenarios of roughly $250M FDV (Ethena-comparable) or $105M FDV (Maple-comparable)
